restartAssessment: A real extension-host PID change preserves the dirty native owner and its session-readonly state; explicit cleanup is needed.

In the fast close/reopen development-host fixture native hot exit did not retain the dirty owner. This is an observed fixture result, not a universal claim about production hot exit; private owner recovery remains required.
The Undo sample in the public API probe is not a full T102 single-apply Undo/Redo acceptance. That requirement remains unproven.
sourceInterpretation: The checked current public TextEditorOptions has tabSize, indentSize, insertSpaces, cursorStyle and lineNumbers. The native 1.109.5 FilesConfigurationService keeps one session override per resource; Set replaces it and Reset deletes it. No supported owned readonly lease has been identified in the checked API. This is a feasibility gap, not proof that every possible editor integration is impossible.
remaining: A verified owner-lock mechanism that preserves prior user restrictions, including dirty/split/reopened native views. Existing support mode alone does not satisfy it; version checks do not substitute for a lock.
Move session/draft state, owner snapshots and recovery, protection ownership and domain transitions into ESKA; expose a reusable IDE-independent contract before enabling the BSL adapter.
Production BSL sessions, selection/unavailable-expression UI, explicit Apply/Cancel, unchanged dirty owner on cancel, one-edit Undo/Redo and close-cancellation flow.
Full locked-owner rejection for Explorer/LSP mutations, support/context/source conflicts, independent windows and fail-safe journal recovery.
T103, T104 and T105 remain in the requested sequence after T102; their completion is not claimed.
settingsScope: The override counterexample changes only readonlyInclude in its owned private workspace, then restores exact original settings bytes. No global user settings are changed.

ideAdapterOwns: applying checked plans through native Undo/Redo
architectureRequirement.contract: One core/RPC behavior across IDE adapters; URI schemes are adapter details. Releasing a query restriction must retain independent support and user restrictions.

supportPrototypeScope: The completed test observes the live dirty native editor and the protected filesystem contract separately. Earlier combined view-switching attempts failed an expected reopen edit and an active-editor focus assertion; these logs remain available. Their cause is not claimed as a production defect or as a verified focus fix. Protected-view native typing is covered by the separate existing support-protected-host suite, not newly accepted by this filesystem observation.
